newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo Nikkei ends above 19,000, Deng impact minimal.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo Nikkei ends above 19,000, Deng impact minimal.

text.p: Tokyo stocks surged on Thursday, with the key market index closing above 19,000 for the first time in more than a month on a rally in property-related issues.
Property and bank shares gained ground on a newspaper report that the government may use public funds to buy land formerly owned by failed housing loan firms and other troubled financial firms.
The Tokyo market shrugged off news of the death of China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping on Wednesday evening.
The Nikkei average of 225 leading issues rose 452.59 points or 2.43 percent to 19,051.71. It last closed above 19,000 on January 6, the first trading day of this year.
Its March futures added 420 points to 19,070.

Tokyo share prices surged in the morning on a report by the influential financial daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun that that the government plans to use more public funds to buy collateralised land now being held loan-collecting bodies.
